name: smoke-cml-pair
description: Harness acceptance test: transient/eye measurement + bit-rate axis plumbing, against a bare 3.3 V NMOS (nfet_03v3) differential pair with the DR-0002 load topology (10 mA tail, 50 ohm/leg to the 3.3 V rail). Not a design deliverable -- issue #11 designs the real CML driver.
claim: None -- harness self-verification, not a spec claim. Proves the transient/rate-axis machinery (tran analysis composition, rate_val parameter plumbing at both spec/tmds-tx.md #1 operating points, raw ngspice `meas` threshold-crossing measurements, and the transient-solver-settings record fields) actually takes effect, so later records against ratified spec lines can be trusted.

measure.trise_10_90: TRIG v(vdiff) VAL=-0.4 RISE=1 TARG v(vdiff) VAL=0.4 RISE=1
measure.tfall_10_90: TRIG v(vdiff) VAL=0.4 FALL=1 TARG v(vdiff) VAL=-0.4 FALL=1

swing_diff_v.description: DR-0002 single-ended swing target 400-600 mV; measured as the peak |outp-outn| excursion

vcm_v.description: DR-0002 common-mode target 2.8-3.3 V at nominal 3.3 V supply; widened here to 2.5-3.7 V because common-mode tracks vdd_val directly through the 50 ohm pull-up and this smoke run sweeps the mandated +/-10% supply axis -- this is a harness-plumbing sanity bound, not a DR-0002 compliance claim (that is issue #11's job at the real driver's operating point)

trise_10_90.description: sanity bound only (this smoke pair's bandwidth is not a spec claim) -- proves the meas-based rise-time measurement actually resolves a sub-UI edge at 742.5 Mbps (UI = 1.347 ns)
